title: Governing at Machine Speed: An Adaptive Intelligence Architecture for Real-Time AI Policy Enforcement
abstract: arXiv:2609.13466v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Enterprise AI adoption has reached 78% of organizations globally, yet the infrastructure to govern that adoption has not kept pace. This paper identifies and characterizes the attestation deficit, a structural condition in which organizations maintain governance policies but cannot produce auditable, tamper-evident evidence of enforcement within regulatory timelines. Drawing on empirical data from the Stanford 2026 AI Index Report (362 documented incidents), the IBM/Ponemon 2026 Cost of a Data Breach study (USD 4.99M average cost, 92% lacking access controls), and the EY/AIUC-1 Consortium survey (38% end-to-end monitoring, 17% agent-to-agent coverage), this paper demonstrates that the governance failure is organizational and architectural rather than technical. translated_title: 以机器速度治理：面向实时AI策略执行的自适应智能架构
translated_abstract: 企业AI的采用率已达到全球78%的组织，但用于治理这种采用的基础设施却未能跟上步伐。本文识别并刻画了“证明缺口”（attestation deficit）这一结构性问题，即组织虽然制定了治理政策，但无法在监管时限内产生可审计的、防篡改的执行证据。基于斯坦福2026年AI指数报告（362起记录在案的事件）、IBM/Ponemon 2026年数据泄露成本研究（平均成本499万美元，92%缺乏访问控制）以及EY/AIUC-1联盟调查（38%实现端到端监控，17%实现代理间覆盖）的实证数据，本文证明了这种治理失败是组织层面和架构层面的问题，而非技术层面的问题。为解决这一缺口，我们提出了AGIL（自适应治理智能层），这是一个概念性的五层架构，旨在利用机器学习实现实时AI治理。
tldr: 本文识别了企业AI治理中的“证明缺口”问题，证明治理失败源于组织和架构层面而非技术层面，并提出AGIL五层自适应智能架构，利用机器学习实现实时的AI政策执行与治理。
en_tdlr: This paper identifies the "attestation deficit" in enterprise AI governance, demonstrates that the governance failure is organizational and architectural rather than technical, and proposes AGIL, a five-layer adaptive intelligence architecture that leverages machine learning for real-time AI policy enforcement.
